objective.statement: Generate ideas by 6-3-5 brainwriting: 36 writers in 6 groups of 6, each adding 3 ideas per pass, sheets rotating for 5 passes - with a mechanical check that later entries BUILD ON the earlier ones rather than restating them.
objective.charter: Brainwriting is silent and written: each writer adds three ideas to a sheet, then the sheet rotates. The value is cumulative - pass 4 should be building on what passes 1 to 3 put on that sheet. That is also the failure mode, because a writer can trivially satisfy the quota by rephrasing the entry above. So the build-on relation is checked MECHANICALLY: an n-gram overlap test between successive entries on the same sheet, with a floor (it must overlap enough to be building on) and a ceiling (not so much that it is a restatement). No evidence citation is required here - this is pure generation, and requiring anchors at this stage would collapse the idea rate for no gain.
success_criteria: all 5 passes completed on every sheet
the n-gram overlap check ran between every pair of successive entries
entries flagged as restatements rather than build-ons are merged or rejected, not counted as novel
the surviving unique-idea count is reported after deduplication, not before

sequence.custom_name: P22 brainwriting 6-3-5: 6 groups of 6 writers, 3 ideas per writer per pass, sheets rotate, 5 passes, silent throughout
n-gram overlap test between successive entries on each sheet: floor proves building-on, ceiling rejects restatement

all_of.producer: sheet ledger: counts completed rotation passes per sheet and reports the minimum across all 6 sheets
all_of.note: DIAL 1 of 2 - the 6-3-5 pass count. Reported as the MINIMUM across sheets, not the mean: a mean would let one finished sheet mask an abandoned one.

all_of.producer: n-gram overlap test between successive entries on the same sheet, with a build-on floor and a restatement ceiling
all_of.note: DIAL 2 of 2 - the design's minimum-deliberation floor, and the only thing separating real brainwriting from 540 paraphrases. The thresholds live in the producer; targets.dedup.max_similarity (0.75) is the restatement ceiling.

metadata.title: Brainwriting 6-3-5 (36 writers, 6 sheets, 5 passes)
metadata.notes: WHEN TO USE: when you want CUMULATIVE ideas - each pass building on the last - and when spoken deliberation would let one loud seat set the frame. The silence is the feature. WHEN NOT TO USE: when you need breadth rather than depth (C-X47's independent fan-out beats it) or when ideas must be anchored - citation is off here by design. The design's named dials are group_size and passes. EDITABLE DIALS: /participants/count/exact_n and /protocol/sequence/0/rounds (group_size x groups, and passes - 6 groups x 6 writers x 3 ideas x 5 passes = 540 raw, which is targets.raw_ideas; changing either number means changing raw_ideas too), /targets/dedup/max_similarity (the restatement ceiling), /budgets/time_minutes. STOPPING (human form): custom:passes_complete >= 5 AND custom:build_on_overlap_checked == true. source_expression absent per the collision proven by _probe_sem_rule_collision.py. SCHEMA LIMITATION worth knowing: the 6-groups-of-6 structure is expressed in the protocol stage rather than in topology.committees, because topology.committees requires named participant_ids and this council auto-composes its 36 seats. The schema can therefore only express group structure over an EXPLICIT roster - an auto-composed swarm must carry its grouping in the protocol, where no validator checks it. Note also that outcomes.allowed is a single value (decision), faithfully following the design card, which means this council has no vocabulary for 'the sweep failed' - if that matters to you, add no_decision.
